locator.section: 8.9 Decompositions of cyclic structures ("Three bonds cleaved")

evidence.curator_note: Substrate is the 3,3,5-trimethylcyclohexanone molecular ion; the page prints '+.' on the carbonyl oxygen with the C=O drawn intact, so the precursor mapped_smiles localizes charge and odd electron on O(1) (O+ with a double bond and no other ligand carries the one unpaired electron). Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the odd electron on O(1) into the C(2)-O(1) bond; drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from the ring C(2)-C(7) sigma bond into that same C-O bond, which therefore rises from double to triple (acylium). The undrawn move 3 carries the second electron of the cleaved ring bond onto C(7); the book prints the radical dot there in the next structure. The cleaved bond is in the ring, so this step only OPENS the ring, giving the distonic acylium .CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-C(CH3)2-CH2-C(triple bond)O+. Map numbers: 1 = O, 2 = carbonyl C, 3 = the retained alpha CH2 (later H donor), 4 = the gem-dimethyl quaternary carbon, 5 = the CH2 between it and C(6), 6 = the methine bearing the lone ring methyl, 7 = the alpha carbon cleaved off the carbonyl, 8/9 = the gem-dimethyl methyls, 10 = the C(6) methyl, 11 = the migrating hydrogen (isotope-tagged [1H:11] so it can carry an atom map; RDKit folds an untagged mapped H into implicit valence).

locator.section: 8.9 Decompositions of cyclic structures ("Three bonds cleaved")

evidence.curator_note: The arrow is labelled 'rH' on the page. Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the radical dot on the terminal carbon C(7) reaching left to the hydrogen the book writes out explicitly as 'H' on C(3); drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from that C(3)-H bond back to C(7), into the C(7)-H bond being formed. The undrawn move 3 leaves the second electron of the old C(3)-H bond on C(3), where the next structure simply shows the dot. Net: a 1,5-hydrogen shift (six-membered transition state C7-C6-C5-C4-C3 plus the H) that moves the radical site next to the acylium carbon while the terminal CH2. becomes CH3.

locator.section: 8.9 Decompositions of cyclic structures ("Three bonds cleaved")

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the radical on C(3) into the forming C(3)=C(4) pi bond; drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from the C(4)-C(5) sigma bond into that same pi bond. The undrawn move 3 puts the second electron of the cleaved C(4)-C(5) bond on C(5); the book just draws the expelled fragment with its dot, an isobutyl (2-methylpropyl) radical, C4H9.. Products: the conjugated acylium (CH3)2C=CH-C(triple bond)O+ at m/z 83 (100%, the ion labelled on the page) plus C4H9.. Three bonds have been cleaved in total (the ring C-C, the C-H and this C-C), matching the 'Three bonds cleaved' heading under which the page places this equation, and the product is the heteroatom-stabilized EE+ ion the text says is 'quite useful for structural characterization'. The migrating hydrogen [1H:11] departs with the isobutyl radical, so the ion is one hydrogen lighter than a hypothetical H-free two-bond ring cleavage would give; that is recorded as hydrogen_shift = -1.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for equation 8.64 (chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14); no MOD rule variable is cross-linked. The obvious candidate for the first step is the generic carbonyl alpha-cleavage IMS_4_14 (DFS '[C]1([C]2[C]3)([C]4[C]5){=}[O+.]>>[C.]2[C]3.[C]4[C]5[C]1{#}[O+]'), and it was CHECKED, not assumed. Its LEFT pattern DOES match this substrate (RDKit: SMARTS [#6](-[#6]-[#6])(-[#6]-[#6])=[O+] -> 1 match, mapping the two branches onto the two ring directions), but the rule is MIS-ENCODED and therefore does not describe this alpha-cleavage: on the left C(1) is bonded to C(2) and C(4), while on the right the acylium carbon C(1) is written bonded to C(5) - so besides breaking the intended C(1)-C(2) bond it also breaks C(1)-C(4) and invents a new C(1)-C(5) bond, i.e. it cleaves a bond that is not the drawn one and re-bonds the acylium to the wrong carbon. The same defect is recorded for equation 8.58. No indexed rule covers the subsequent 1,5-rH between two carbons of a distonic acylium, nor the final beta C-C cleavage (IMS_4_33_alpha_1 is the closest charge-retention alpha step but is authored for an enol oxocarbenium with the charge on a hydroxyl oxygen, not for an acylium). The page prints '100%' beside m/z 83 as a bare percentage without naming the experiment; it is the book's standard 70 eV EI value (running head '8 / Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation') and ms_context is set accordingly.
